meta.title: Aikido etiquette
meta.description: Rules of conduct in the dojo and on the tatami. Ethical principles of aikido – greetings, bows, proper sitting, safety rules.

header.title: Etiquette
header.subtitle: Rules of conduct in the dojo

ethics: When entering the dojo and stepping onto the tatami, bow toward the portrait of the founder of aikido.
Meditation at the beginning and end of training serves for preparation and integration.
When entering, use the greeting "onegaishimas(u)" and at the end "domo arigatou gozaimash(i)ta".
At the beginning and end of practice with a partner, bow to each other.
rules: Late arrival requires waiting at the edge of the tatami and an invitation from the instructor.
Early departure or interruption must be reported to the instructor.
Proper sitting: seiza or cross-legged with a straight back.
It is not allowed to sit with your back to the kamiza or with legs stretched out.
tatami: Do not wear jewelry (rings, earrings, necklaces) for safety reasons.
Food, drinks, or mobile phones are not allowed on the tatami.
Maintain cleanliness – clean gi, trimmed nails.
quote: All of these rules have their purpose and help us create an atmosphere of concentration and growth on the tatami.
